title: A negative-control outcome for transport bias
question: Can a negative-control outcome detect and calibrate transport bias in an unanchored MAIC, and when does the calibration fail?
design: Unanchored MAIC with an unmeasured covariate shifted between populations, a negative-control outcome sharing some, all or more of its prognostic dependence, and effect modification absent or present; naive, control-test and calibrated contrasts. 16 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: Only in a knife-edge case. A negative-control outcome with no treatment effect detects a population difference (flag rate up to 0.83) but calibrates the primary contrast correctly only when its dependence on the unmeasured covariate equals the primary outcome's and that covariate does not modify the treatment effect (bias 0.001). Otherwise the calibrated contrast was biased by -0.18 to 0.40: it missed the modification part, overcorrected with a more strongly dependent control, and cancelled by coincidence in one scenario.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: calibrated bias -0.183 to 0.399 wherever the control's bias differed from the primary's.
Control test size 0.039 to 0.056 without a shift; power 0.04 to 0.83 with a 0.5 SD shift, rising with the control's dependence on the unmeasured covariate.
With modification by the unmeasured covariate and a matched control, calibration left 0.19 of 0.41 naive bias.
not_answered: One control outcome rather than a bank with empirical calibration; unanchored only; availability of control outcomes not surveyed. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Marginal log odds ratio of the primary outcome, B versus A, in the target
